text.p: Interstate Hotels Co chief executive W. Thomas Parrington said on Wednesday that he was "comfortable" with analysts' estimates for the company's second quarter earnings, which First Call consensus placed at $0.33 per share, but that he did not expect a new leasing agreement to boost the results.

"This will have no impact at all on the second quarter (performance)," Parrington told Reuters, referring to a long-term lease agreement for 27 Hampton Inns hotels from Equity Inns Inc, announced earlier in the day.

However, Parrington said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates for the fiscal second quarter, which will end on June 30. The hotel managing company expects to release its second quarter results the week of July 21.
No comparable earnings figures were available for the year-ago period because Intersate, the largest U.S. hotel management company, only went public in June 1996.
Parrington added that the leasing agreement came too late in the quarter to affect results.
But Michael Rietbrock, an analyst with Smith Barney, disagreed.

"The leasing agreement will clearly add to earnings per share, although we probably won't change our formal estimates at this point," Rietbrock said. Smith Barney estimates Interstate will post second quarter earnings of $0.32 a share.
"Interstate is a hidden gem in the hotel industry," Rietbrock added.
He noted that while Interstate may not have a hotel brand name that makes it easy to recognize for consumers, investors were becoming more familiar with the company.
"The industry's doing great and this is a great balanced growth story within it," Rietbrock said.

In keeping with a strategy to lease middle-market hotels and acquire from the high end of the market, Interstate said on Wednesday that it had entered into a long-term lease agreement for 27 Hampton Inns from the Equity Inns real estate investment trust.
With the new leasing agreemement, Interstate said it owns or has a controlling interest in 32 hotels, while it owns, manages, leases or performs services for 229 facilities.

"We've had a strategy to get more heavily involved in the middle market," said Parrington. In such agreements, "the base rent due is a low percentage of actual cash flows," he said, "We have minimum risk in doing this."
Interstate traded at 29-3/4, up 5/8 from Tuesday's 29-1/8 close.
